questions.question: You see heavy smoke ahead on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beam headlights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Move as far right as you can and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can hurt your eyes and lungs or be deadly.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other driver is on your left. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You.
Whoever is signaling a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You are entering an interstate using a short ramp with no acceleration lane. What should you do?

options.text: Enter the right lane right away and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you see an open gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you see an open gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic. Then speed up and merge. You should stay stopped while waiting for a safe gap.

questions.question: A tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the wheel tight and brake lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel tight and brake lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using light braking. Do not stop on the road. Pull off in a safe place.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have left the pavement. What is the first thing you should do?

options.text: Turn the wheels slightly left to get back on the pavement.
Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently. Slow down, check for traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: When must you give the right-of-way to pedestrians?

options.text: When they are in a marked crosswalk.
When they are in any crosswalk or intersection.
When they are crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, yield to anyone crossing the street.

questions.question: When is the road most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain is just starting.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain is just starting.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain just begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a slick surface.

questions.question: Streets and highways are most slippery:

options.text: After heavy rain for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after rain starts.
questions.explanation: The first half hour of rain is dangerous. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not yet washed away, making roads very slippery. Drive slowly on wet roads.

questions.question: You cannot see other vehicles because of dust or smoke. You should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever conditions make it hard to see other vehicles. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer a middle course between them.

questions.question: When traffic is moving 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to the traffic around you (within posted limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot crash into each other. Accidents happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn permitted on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light and have not yet entered the intersection, stop your vehicle safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, look for a:

options.text: Two- to three-second gap in traffic.
Three- to four-second gap in traffic.
Four- to five-second gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four- to five-second gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check for traffic in the lane you want to enter. Look for a four- to five-second gap, use your turn signal, and check your blind spot. Adjust your speed and move into the lane. Watch for other vehicles doing the same.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This helps the vehicle roll off the road instead of toward traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous because you cannot see as far. Increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead to avoid a crash if it stops suddenly. Use your headlights properly and follow the rules for high and low beams.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right (toward the road edge). This makes the vehicle roll off the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Moving to the right edge of the road as much as possible and stopping.
Moving into the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to the right edge of the road as much as possible and stopping.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop, but do not stop in an intersection. You can drive again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle. Look ahead, to the sides, and behind you. This helps you see problems early and change your speed or position if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, you must know where traffic is. Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see all traffic around you.

questions.question: If you can only see 100 feet ahead due to rain, snow, dust, smoke, or fog, what is the safest speed?

options.text: 20 mph.
30 mph.
40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Bad weather reduces how far you can see. If you can only see 100 feet ahead, do not drive faster than 30 mph.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Drive at normal speed.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car skids.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on wet roads causes your tires to lose grip and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning. The best way to prevent it is to drive slowly in rain or wet conditions.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and safe for turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching.
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
Proceed carefully through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. Then proceed only when it is safe to do so.
